You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Birchwood wayfinding","question":"Can the clerk mark installation complete for the northern signs?","claims":{"A":"The signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day.","B":"The signs were made of wood.","C":"The signs were delivered on Thursday."},"handoff":"{\"claims\":{\"A\":{\"status\":\"unresolved\",\"citations\":[\"S3\"]},\"B\":{\"status\":\"contradicted\",\"citations\":[\"S2\"]},\"C\":{\"status\":\"supported\",\"citations\":[\"S1\"]}},\"note\":\"S1 confirms signs were delivered Thursday, supporting claim C. S2 lists aluminium signs, contradicting claim B that signs were wooden. S3 details intended orientation and approval without photo but does not confirm actual mounting facing paths on opening day, leaving claim A unresolved.\"}","follow_up":{"S4":"an independent time-stamped opening-day survey shows one of the four signs facing away from the path."}}

Thus, claim A is contradicted by S4, claim B is contradicted by S2, and claim C is supported by S1."}

parsed.note: The follow-up source S4 provides direct evidence that at least one sign was facing away from the path on opening day, contradicting claim A that all signs were mounted facing the paths. S2 confirms the signs are aluminium, contradicting claim B that they were wooden. S1 confirms the signs were delivered on Thursday, supporting claim C. Thus, claim A is contradicted by S4, claim B is contradicted by S2, and claim C is supported by S1.
